newsitem.title: EGYPT: Damascus Declaration ministers gather in Cairo.
newsitem.headline: Damascus Declaration ministers gather in Cairo.

text.p: The foreign ministers of Egypt, Syria and the six Gulf Arab states meet in Cairo from Saturday evening to discuss the Middle East peace process and Gulf security and stability, officials said.
The eight countries, known as the Damascus Declaration states after the loose alliance they signed after the Gulf War in 1991, meet every six months to keep the alliance alive.

United Arab Emirates (UAE) Foreign Minister Rashid Abdullah al-Nuaimi, arriving in Cairo on Friday evening, said the two-day meeting would also discuss relations with Iraq and his country's dispute with Iran over three Gulf islands.
"Arab national security is suffering from two problems -- the Israeli occupation of Arab territory and Iranian occupation of UAE territory," Nuaimi told reporters at Cairo airport.
"The Declaration states...are always working to recover these lands and ensure Arab national security," he added.
"The Iraqi people is suffering a lot and common Arab work should be done (in that regard)," Nuaimi said. "But the prime responsibility lies on the Iraqi government.
"We hope it confesses it has committed a crime against Kuwait... We do not want an Iraq which we fear, but a brotherly Iraq which we trust," the minister added.

Since the last Damascus Declaration meeting in Muscat in July, Gulf Arab have again criticised Iran, while Iraq has reached agreement with the United Nations on limited Iraqi oil exports to pay for imports of food and medicine.

An annual Gulf summit in Doha this month called on Iran to leave the three Gulf islands claimed by the UAE and criticised Tehran's military development programme and deployment of surface-to-surface missiles.

A Qatari official said on Wednesday that on the sidelines of the Cairo meeting the Gulf ministers - from Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates -- would discuss a border dispute between Qatar and Bahrain.

"The meeting (in Cairo) will try to narrow the differences between the two neighbours and stop the open war of words... The meeting will be held within the framework of the recent decision by the Doha summit," the official told Reuters.
A Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) summit in the Qatari capital Doha this month, boycotted by Bahrain, decided to set up a committee to resolve the rift between the two Gulf states.
Bahrain and Qatar have been adds for decades over a cluster of small islands and sandbanks in the Gulf, controlled by Bahrain since the 1930s but also claimed by Qatar.
Qatar has taken the case to the International Court of Justice in The Hague. The move has angered Bahrain, which prefers a regional solution.
Tension rose when Bahrain accused a Qatari man and woman of spying and sentenced them on Wednesday to three years in prison.
Qatar had accused Manama earlier of supporting an anti-government plot, which Doha said it had foiled in February.
